<entry id="A01208">
<head-word>אִיטָא, </head-word>
<head-word>אִיטָה, </head-word>
<hw-number>I</hw-number>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (ἦτα) 
<italic>the letter</italic> (η) of the Greek Alphabet, the numerical value of which is 
<italic>eight</italic>
<italic>;</italic> used in the way of a phonetic play (ἤτω, or ἰτά as though an adj. verbale of ἰέναι) to indicate 
<italic>going</italic> or 
<italic>death</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 14, beg. (proving that a seven months’ child can live, while an eight months’ child cannot) מדידכון אנא ממטי איט"א אוכ"טא, לכון זיט"א אפ"טא from your own (Greek) language I will prove it to you, ‘
<italic>Live</italic> (ζήτω) 
<italic>seven, Go, eight</italic>’ (ζ = ἕπτα, η = ὄκτω). Y. Yeb. IV, 5
<sup>d</sup> top; Tanḥ. B’midbar 18 (corr. acc.); Ibid. (ed. Buber) 21.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>

<italic>thick, heavy</italic>,] 
<italic>lamb</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Gen. XXX, 32; a. fr.—Ned. I, 3 ‘this be as forbidden to me כאימרא (Y. ib. I, end, 37

<italic>the</italic> lamb’—כאימר תמידא that means, ‘as the lamb of the daily offering’. Lam. R. introd. (R. Josh. </notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> דהוה נכיס אמ' וכ' who slaughters a lamb and augurs from its liver.</definition>
<notes> Erub. 53
<sup>b</sup> (deriding the Galilean dialect) a Galilean cried אמר למאן וכ' who wants 
<italic>amar?</italic> (indistinctly pronouncing the vowels, as well as the guttural sound of א), when they said to him …, חמר למירכב או חמר למשתי עמר למילבש או אימר לאיתכסאה (for var. lect., v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 10) do you mean 
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>ǎmâr</italic> (an ass) to ride on, or 
<italic>ḥ</italic>
<italic>ămar</italic> (wine) to drink, or 
<italic>ãmar</italic> (wool) for putting on, or 
<italic>immar</italic> (lamb) for slaughtering?; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. אִימְּרִין, אִימְּרַיָּא, אִימְּרַיָּיה, אִמְּ'</plural-form>. Ezra VII, 9; a. e.—Targ. Ex. XXIX, 38; XII, 5; a. e.—Y. Snh. I, 18
<sup>d</sup> top אי' רכיכין the lambs (of the spring) are yet tender (in a letter announcing the intercalation of a month); Bab. ib. 11
<sup>b</sup> א' עדקין (not ער'; v. Tosef. ib. II, 6); a. e.—Fem. אִימַּרְתָּא 
<italic>ewe</italic>. Targ. Lev. V, 6; a. e.—Ḥull. 51
<sup>a</sup>. Gen. R. s. 44 end, the sow (Rome) pastures with twenty (young ones), וא' ולא בחד and the ewe (Sarah) not even with one.—2) (cmp. חוּמְרָא) 
<italic>knot, bandage</italic> on wounds. Snh. 98
<sup>a</sup> כולהו שרי ואסרי אי' וכ' Ar. (in ed. a. Ms. our w. omitted) all of them untie their bandages all at once and tie them up all at once, but he attends to one at a time.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>fringe, border</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ps. CXXXIII, 2. Targ. Y. Ex. XXVI, 4 (Var. אֶימְרָא). V. next w.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—4)</number>
<definition>* 
<pos> pr. n. pl.</pos> כפר א' 
<italic>K’far Imra</italic> (Lamb-ville).</definition>
<notes> Y. Taan. IV, 69
<sup>a</sup> bot.; (Lam. R. to II, 2 נמרא).</notes></sense></senses></entry>
